# Scope
Screen Layout Configurator (SLC) – Company-Level Scope
The configurator applies to the Sales Order module and governs:
• Field visibility
• Field mandatory/non-mandatory behaviour
• Field caption customization
These configurations will be applied dynamically to Sales Order screens based on the defined setup.
The View Configurator allows authorized users to create, manage, and assign multiple screen views based on business needs, while ensuring compliance with the constraints defined by the SLC.
Sales Order List & Creation
This specification covers UI-level enhancements for the Sales Order List screen only. The scope includes:
• Improved filtering and navigation options for easier identification of relevant sales orders.
• Enhanced visibility of key order, delivery, and style-level details directly from the list view.
• Quick-access mechanisms to drill down into delivery and style information without additional navigation.
• A configurable provision to display either:
• The top 50 transactions, or
• Only user-created transactions,
in alignment with the current system functionality.
Permission & Setting
This SSRS defines how system permissions regulate user actions across the Sales Order lifecycle, including:
• Creation, revision, viewing, and reopening of Sales Orders
• Field-level edit permissions (price, quantity, delivery dates, shipment mode, payment terms, etc.)
• Exception handling and approval routing for restricted changes
• Role-based access to cancellation, closure, deletion, and logging actions

# Purpose

### Screen Layout Configurator
• To maintain standardization of the Sales Order screen across the organization.
• To ensure compliance with business rules and process guidelines.
• To create a baseline layout for all subsequent user-level configurations.

### View Configurator
The View Configurator provides an additional layer of customization on top of the Screen Layout Configurator (SLC). While the SLC defines the global structure and rules, the View Configurator enables user-, role-, or department-level personalization of Sales Order screens to support different operational workflows.
• To provide flexibility and personalization without breaking company-wide standards.
• To support diverse operational workflows within the same company.
• To enable efficient screen usage based on job function.

### Sales Order List & Creation
The purpose of this specification is to define the UI enhancement requirements for the Sales Order List screen. The objective is to improve user efficiency and decision-making by enhancing filtering capabilities, navigation flow, data visibility, and quick access to delivery- and style-level information. These enhancements aim to reduce search time, improve clarity, and maintain consistency with existing system behaviour.

### User Permission & Setting’s
The purpose of this System Scope & Requirement Specification (SSRS) is to define, document, and govern system behavior, user permissions, and configuration-driven controls related to Sales Orders (OC) and associated processes within the garment export ERP system.
This document establishes how the system will:
• Enforce role-based permissions
• Control editable and non-editable actions
• Drive approval workflows
• Handle business validations and restrictions
• Differentiate between current scope and future phase (Phase-II) enhancements
The SSRS ensures that all Sales Order–related operations comply with defined business rules, audit requirements, and operational governance standards.

# Solution

## 1. Screen Layout Configurator (SLC)
The SLC serves as the foundation for all Sales Order screen configurations. It defines the global structure and rules that apply across the entire company.

### 1.1 Key Capabilities
• Global Field Visibility Control
• Administrators can configure which fields should be visible, hidden, or optional.
• These rules apply company-wide, ensuring consistent behaviour for all users.
• Global Caption Customization
• SLC includes the ability to change the caption or display name of any field.
• This supports industry-specific terminology or localized naming requirements.
• Uniform UI Structure
• The SLC determines the default layout of the Sales Order screen.
• Controls the sequence of fields, grouping, or panel structure (if applicable).
• Company-Level Enforcement
• Once activated for a company, all users inherit the same base layout.
• Individual users cannot override SLC settings unless permitted via the View Configurator.
Screen will be design like this: -
Path: - Admin Configurator Screen Layout Configurator
System will show the WFX Page- Sales Order and List Type option should be Sales Order New & Sales Order List. Object and level will be coming system based as it is working right now.
After Clicking on Setup icon system will open the setup configuration
The Screen Layout Configurator (SLC) is designed to provide a configurable framework for Sales Order screens. It allows authorized users to control the visibility, mandatory status, and caption (label) of fields displayed on the Sales Order screen, ensuring flexibility while maintaining global consistency.
The SLC serves as the foundation for all Sales Order screen configurations and defines the global structure and rules applicable across the organization.

### 1.2 SLC Capabilities
For each field defined in the SLC, the following configuration options must be available:
• Visibility
• Visible
• Hidden
• Mandatory Indicator
• Mandatory
• Non-Mandatory
(Applicable only if the field is visible)
• Caption Customization
• We don’t need any provision to change a UI caption. If user need to do then they will use the multi-lingual setup to change the caption in system language.
• Field placement
• Ability to modify the placement of the field.
• Edit
• This option allows to user edit the column permission.

### 1.3 Global Configuration Level
The SLC operates at a global level, meaning:
• Configurations apply across the entire company
• Acts as the base configuration for all Sales Order screens
• Subsequent configurations (if any) will inherit rules from the SLC

Field Behaviour & Validation Rules
1. Order Season
• The Order Season field will always be auto-populated from the user profile.
• The field will be non-editable during Sales Order Creation.
2. Payment Terms
• The mandatory behaviour of Payment Terms depends on the Order Type:
• If Order Type = Provisional or Projection
→ Payment Terms will be non-mandatory.
• For all other Order Types
→ Payment Terms will be mandatory.
3. Consignee Address
• The mandatory behaviour of Consignee Address depends on the Order Type:
• If Order Type = Provisional or Projection
→ Consignee Address will be non-mandatory.
• For all other Order Types
→ Consignee Address will be mandatory.
4. LC Number
• The LC Number field will be mandatory only when:
Payment Type = LC
• For all other payment types, the field will remain optional.
5. OC Factory
• If Order Type = CM:
• The label “OC Factory” will be renamed to “Supplier”.
• The field will become mandatory.
• For all other Order Types:
• The field will retain the label “OC Factory”.
• The field will remain optional (unless defined otherwise).
6. OC Delivery Date
• OC Delivery Date will always be auto-populated with the Buyer Delivery Date.
• Manual modification of this field will not be allowed unless explicitly permitted by configuration.
7. Bill To
• The Bill To field will be auto-populated from the Buyer Master.
• The system will select the address that is marked as “Bill To = Yes”.
• If multiple addresses are marked, system behaviour should follow the predefined priority rule.
The default SLC (Sales Order New Configuration) columns for the Sales Order New should be visibility type always in the above given table. It means when we don’t make any SLC and View configurator for sales order creation and list UI then system have to set these field as a default and load these fields at the time of UI opening.

1.4 Validation Rules
• Mandatory fields must be populated before Sales Order submission.
• Hidden fields must not be displayed on the UI and should not be validated.
• Caption changes must reflect consistently across all relevant Sales Order screens.
• When SLC is defined, it becomes the default screen layout for all users.

## 2. View Configurator – User/Department-Level

#### 2.1 Personalized or Department-Specific Views
In the list type we need two options: -
1. Sales Order New: For the Sales Order Creation Transaction.
2. Sales Order List: For the Sales Order List UI.
Sales Order List: -
Sales Order New: -
• The system shall allow the creation of multiple views for the same Sales Order New & Sales Order List.
• In this we have given a field of buyer which will be mandatory in case of List type -Sales order New only. For the Sales Order List it should be blank.
• Buyer Field: We can select multiple buyer in the list of single view. System should not allow to created multiple view for a single buyer.
• Buyer dropdown should be multi select, System should allow to create the view for multiple buyer.
• The permitted buyer should be come in the dropdown of buyer name.
• In this we have given two toggler options which will work on this sales order list and filter the data on it accordingly.
• Created Order Permission: - It means the system will show the record based on the creation of the logged in user
• Created Order & Buyer wise permission: - It means system will show the record based on the creation of logged in user and also show the permit buyer creation record.
• Default: If we don’t define any config for any user then system will always show as per current working structure of our List UI function.
Note: System should allow to toggle any one of it.
• Each view can be tailored to suit specific workflows or departmental requirements.
• Different teams may have different views based on their operational focus.
• Example:
• Sales Team views may emphasize pricing and commercial fields.
• Support or Operations teams may focus on customer, delivery, or compliance-related fields.
• This tree will work based on the click on their group, suppose we will click on the other information then system will filter out the respective of those fields only.

#### 2.2 User / Role / Department-Based Assignment
• Views can be assigned to one or more of the following:
• Individual users
• User groups, Departments & Role wise
• A user may have access to multiple views depending on assigned permissions.
• In the Sales Order Creation screen, multiple views can be assigned to a user under the program permissions for Sales Order – New. Once the user selects the Buyer in the transaction, the system will apply the relevant views based on the assigned permissions.
• In the Sales Order List, only one view permission can be assigned to a user at a time.

#### 2.3 Permission-Based Access Control
• The system shall provide administrative controls to manage permissions for the View Configurator.
• Administrators can define which users have the ability to:
• Create new views
• Modify existing views
• Assign views based on their user’s group, roles or departments
• Switch between available views
• Users without appropriate permissions will only be able to use assigned views.
• After view permission is granted, the user will be able to see the List Type names based on their assigned permissions.
For example, if a user is granted access to the View Configurator, the system must validate whether the user also has permission for Sales Order Creation and Sales Order List. Based on this permission check, the system will display only those List Type names for which the user has the required access rights, ensuring that users can view details strictly according to their permissions.
Permission should be driven through below given screenshot.
After Click on Divv >> system will open the view permission pop-up where user can set the view permissions accordingly.
Note: - In case of Sales Order Creation: It should be checkbox option for selecting multiple view.
For Sales Order list: It should be radio button, user can permit only one view for a user.

#### 2.4 Field-Level Customization (Within SLC Constraints)
• Authorized users may customize fields within the limits defined by the SLC.
• Customization options include:
• Field visibility (only for fields enabled in SLC)
• Field caption changes (if allowed by SLC)
• Field order Sequencing
• Section arrangement, where applicable

#### 2.5 Multiple View Support
• The system shall support multiple views per user.
• Users can switch between assigned views based on their current task or activity.
• The default view will be the one defined by the SLC unless:
• A specific view is assigned to the user, role, or department, and
• The user has permission to use or switch to that view.

Field Behaviour & Validation Rules
1. Order Season
• The Order Season field will always be auto-populated from the user profile.
• The field will be non-editable during Sales Order Creation.
2. Payment Terms
• The mandatory behaviour of Payment Terms depends on the Order Type:
• If Order Type = Provisional or Projection
→ Payment Terms will be non-mandatory.
• For all other Order Types
→ Payment Terms will be mandatory.
3. Consignee Address
• The mandatory behaviour of Consignee Address depends on the Order Type:
• If Order Type = Provisional or Projection
→ Consignee Address will be non-mandatory.
• For all other Order Types
→ Consignee Address will be mandatory.
4. LC Number
• The LC Number field will be mandatory only when:
Payment Type = LC
• For all other payment types, the field will remain optional.
5. OC Factory
• If Order Type = CM:
• The label “OC Factory” will be renamed to “Supplier”.
• The field will become mandatory.
• For all other Order Types:
• The field will retain the label “OC Factory”.
• The field will remain optional (unless defined otherwise).
6. OC Delivery Date
• OC Delivery Date will always be auto-populated with the Buyer Delivery Date.
• Manual modification of this field will not be allowed unless explicitly permitted by configuration.
7. Bill To
• The Bill To field will be auto-populated from the Buyer Master.
• The system will select the address that is marked as “Bill To = Yes”.
• If multiple addresses are marked, system behaviour should follow the predefined priority rule.
8. Order Type
• It will come in confirmed Order Type.
The default SLC (Sales Order New Configuration) columns for the Sales Order New should be visibility type always in the above given table. It means when we don’t make any SLC and View configurator for sales order creation and list UI then system have to set these field as a default and load these fields at the time of UI opening.
In the flex field section, we have provided the detail from “OC GMPO Sales ASN RMPO ASN GMPO”.
Sales Order Creation – Buyer-Based View Permission Logic
Objective
To ensure that, during Sales Order Creation, the system displays the appropriate View based on:
• The selected Buyer
• The user’s assigned view permissions
Configuration Assumptions
• Multiple Buyer-specific Views can be configured in Sales Order – New (Program Permission).
• Each View is mapped to a specific Buyer.
• A user may or may not have permission to access a particular Buyer View.
• Default View is the fall back view when no permitted Buyer-specific view is available.
System Behaviour (Step-by-Step)
• The user opens the Sales Order Creation screen.
• The system loads all views assigned to the user under Sales Order – New permissions.
• The user selects a Buyer in the transaction.
• The system checks:
• Whether a Buyer-specific View exists for the selected Buyer.
• Whether the user has permission = Yes for that View.
• Based on this validation, the system determines which view to display.
Expected Result – Buyer-wise Logic
1. Buyer: GAP
• Configured View: SK View
• User Permission: No
• System Action:
• System detects that the Buyer-specific view exists.
• User does not have permission for SK View.
• Result:
• System displays the Default View.
2. Buyer: LEVIS
• Configured View: PK View
• User Permission: Yes
• System Action:
• System detects the Buyer-specific view.
• User has valid permission for PK View.
• Result:
• System displays PK View in Sales Order Creation.
3. Buyer: RED TAPE
• Configured View: RK View
• User Permission: No
• System Action:
• System detects the Buyer-specific view.
• User does not have permission for RK View.
• Result:
• System displays the Default View.

[TABLE 3: Table 3 · 3 rows · columns: Buyer (text), View Name (text), Permission (boolean), Expected Result In Sales Order Creation (text)]
| Buyer | View Name | Permission | Expected Result In Sales Order Creation |
| GAP | SK View | No | Default View |
| LEVIS | PK View | Yes | PK View |
| RED TAPE | RK View | No | Default View |

#### 2.8 Validation and Behaviour Rules
• All view configurations must comply with global rules defined in the SLC.
• Fields marked as hidden or mandatory at the SLC level must retain those properties across all views.
• View changes should take effect immediately upon selection or re-login, as defined by system settings.
• If users are assigned a custom view, the system will:
• Automatically load the assigned view instead of the SLC layout.
• Enforce visibility rules and permissions from the selected view.
• Distinct buyer should always comes in the Buyer name field in the View configurator.
Screen will be design like this: -
Path: - Admin Configurator View Configurator
Overall Goals of the Project
• Provide a dynamic and configurable Sales Order screen adaptable to both organizational and individual needs.
• Ensure consistency through SLC while supporting customization through View Configurator.
• Enhance user productivity by letting different teams tailor views relevant to their daily tasks.
• Improve the system’s flexibility and reduce dependency on development changes for screen customization.

## 3. Sales Order List – UI Enhancement Specification

### 3.0 Overview
This section defines the UI enhancement requirements for the Sales Order List screen, focusing on improved filtering, navigation, visibility, and quick access to delivery and style-level information.
A provision is required to display either the top 50 transactions or only the user-created transactions, in line with the current system functionality.

### 3.1 Sales Order List Screen Layout

#### 3.1.1 Header – Left Section
Components & Behaviour:
• Screen Label: "Sales Order"
• Global Search Filter:
• Allows users to search and filter Sales Orders using any value available in the grid.
Sales Order Number
Style Number
• Selected Row Counter:
• Displays the count of currently selected rows in the grid.

#### 3.1.2 Header – Middle Section
Filters & Sorting:
• Status Filter (Dropdown)
• Filters Sales Orders based on selected order status.
• Buyer Filter (Dropdown)
• Filters Sales Orders based on selected buyer.
• Sort by Created-On Date
• Allows ascending and descending sorting of the grid based on order creation date.

#### 3.1.3 Header – Right Section
Tools & Actions:
• Add New Order
• Opens the Sales Order creation screen.
• Floating Filter
• Allows column-level filtering directly from the grid header.
• Quick Sort (Created-On Date)
• Provides a shortcut to sort records by creation date.

#### 3.1.4 Grid-Level Behaviour

##### a. Row Interaction
• On hover, the grid row is highlighted using the colour defined in the Figma mock-up.
• On row selection:
• The system loads and displays delivery-related data for the selected Sales Order. This will work only the click on Sales Order Number

##### b. Grid Function
User can open the sales order delivery wise data on the click of the row.
There is two behaviour of the grid and based on this the delivery option will work of expand and collapse.
Tools in the view header
• Edit
• Allows the user to revise the selected Sales Order directly from the list screen.
• Full View Mode
• Opens a full-screen, read-only detailed view of the selected Sales Order.
• Close
• To Close the screen.
• Back button
• Expand and Collapse Tool.

##### c. Detailed Presentation
Grid Purpose & Data Scope
• The grid displays Sales Orders based on the user’s assigned roles and permissions.
• By default, the grid shows the most recently created Sales Orders accessible to the logged-in user.
New and Enhanced Columns
• Status: Displayed as a visual progress bar to quickly indicate the current state of each Sales Order.
• Deliveries Count: Shows the total number of deliveries linked to the Sales Order.
• Actions: A dedicated column pinned to the right for quick and consistent access to order-related actions.
• System will always show the grid data based on Sales Order Number and Article wise, it means if we have a one OC and there are multiple article in this then system will show the data in the list Article wise and Sales Order number should be common for all.
Actions Column Behaviour
• Inline Actions:
• Edit – Opens the Sales Order in edit mode.
• Percentage – Displays task or process completion percentage for the Sales Order.
• Context Menu Actions:
• Cancel – Cancels the selected Sales Order.
• Reopen – Reopens a previously cancelled or closed Sales Order.
• Close – Marks the Sales Order as closed.
• Log – Displays the activity and event history of the Sales Order.

##### d. Header Information (Read-Only)
Displayed at the top of the Full View screen:
• Buyer Name
• My Company Name
• Order Creation Date
• Total Order Value
• Total % in the circle based on the Order delivery (Means if we have an order of 100 pcs and we delivered 80 from it then it will so 80%).

#### 3.1.5 Delivery-Level Details
• Displays all deliveries associated with the selected Sales Order.
• Data is presented in a configurable grouping grid.
Grid Characteristics:
• Grouping rules are defined via the View Configurator.
• Only predefined fields are available for grouping.
• Grouped columns are displayed in non-editable (view-only) mode.

#### 3.1.6 Delivery wise Styles Section
The Styles section supports two selectable grid behaviour, controlled via a grid behaviour tool on the right side.

##### 1 Mode A – Style + Color + Size Combination
Behaviour:
• Users can select multiple combinations of Style + Color + Size.
• The system generates one row per unique combination.
Columns:
• Style + Color + Size
• Number of Sets
• Size
• Selling Price
• Value
• Total Quantity

##### 2 Mode B – Style-wise Grouping
Behaviour:
• Users select multiple styles from a dropdown.
• The system creates separate grouped sections for each style.
Columns:
• Color / Size
• Quantity
• Selling Price
• Value
• Total Quantity

## 4. Sales Order Creation Transaction

### 4.1 Transaction Entry Points & Navigation
Users can create or access a Sales Order through the following paths:
• Sales Order List Screen
• A button “Add New Order” is available at the top-right corner.
• Clicking this button opens a new Sales Order transaction.
• Purchase Order from Buyer Screen
• A new menu option allows users to create/open a Sales Order directly from a Buyer Purchase Order.
• Relevant buyer and order reference details are auto-carried forward.

### 4.2 Overall UI Concept
• The Sales Order screen follows a Transactional-based UI.
• Each section is presented logically to guide the user step-by-step.
• Fields are categorized as:
• Always Visible: Mandatory and fixed on screen.
• Optional: Configurable via View Configurator.
• This will open in same page with full view mode.

### 4.3 Main UI Header – Tools & Labels

#### 4.3.1 Header Label
• Screen title: “Sales Order”: This title will be change based on event, like: - if we will be making new sales order through Sales Order new button or revising it through edit button then the title name should be “Add Sales Order” in case of new creation of Sales Order, if we are opening revision mode then it should be “Edit Sales Order” else in view mode it should be only “Sales Order”.

#### 4.3.2 Header Tools
• Confirm
• To confirm the Sales Order transaction.
• Quick Fills - Copy Order (Two Options): - This will help user to fill the Sales order details with using below given two options.
• Copy from Buyer Default Template
• If a predefined template exists in the Buyer Master → Default Tab, the system auto-copies all default values when the buyer is selected.
• In this we are showing the buyer template name.
• System will show the buyer template based on selected buyer only.
• Copy from Existing Sales Order
• User selects an existing Sales Order.
• System copies all details, including quantities.
• In this we are showing Sales Order Number, Style & Order Qty
• Search option: User can search the order based on the Sales Order Number and Style.
• System will show the last 10 order in the list.
• Back Tool

OC Factory Column Behaviour for CM Order Type
The OC Factory column requires modification when the Order Type is selected as CM (Cut & Make).
When the Order Type = CM is selected, the system should rename the “OC Factory” field to “Supplier Name.”
The Supplier Name field should be displayed as a dropdown, with values populated from the Supplier Master.
The dropdown list must be filtered based on the selected category, ensuring that only relevant suppliers are available for selection.
GMPO Creation Logic
Based on the selected Supplier Name, the system should automatically create Garment Purchase Orders (GMPOs).
If the sales order contains multiple deliveries, the system should generate separate GMPOs for each delivery.
This means GMPO creation will be delivery-wise, resulting in multiple GMPOs for the same supplier when deliveries differ.
Summary of Expected Behaviour
Order Type = CM → OC Factory renamed to Supplier Name
Supplier selection sourced from Supplier Master
Supplier list filtered by selected category
GMPOs created automatically
GMPOs generated per delivery, not as a single consolidated order

### 4.7 Article Selection Option
In this we have an option to select any styles from the dropdown for the specific deliveries.
Note: System should always make a TBA colour/size line by default in both grid.

#### 4.7.1 Mode A – Style + Color + Size Combination
• Users can select multiple combinations of Style + Color + Size.
• System creates rows based on each unique combination.
• In this the style dropdown will work based on Style + Color + Size basis.
• Once we will enter the data in any grid type then system will automatically show in the both grid.
• Delete tool no needed.
• Now user can select and de-select the color-size on the click of article-color-size where system will open the below given pop-up.
Columns:
• Style + Color + Size
• Number of Sets
• Size
• Selling Price
• Value
• Total Quantity

#### 4.7.2 Mode B – Style-wise Grouping
• Users select multiple styles from a dropdown.
• System creates separate groups per style.
• In this the style dropdown will work based on Style only.
• We are providing a “Price Per” selection option within the Techpack settings. Based on the selected option, the pricing entry will function as follows:
• Article:
If selected, the system allows the user to enter the price at the article level.
• Color:
If selected, the system opens a color-wise pricing pop-up where the user can define prices for each color. The system will then calculate and display the average price on the main screen.
• Size:
If selected, the system opens a size-wise pricing pop-up where the user can define prices for each size. The system will calculate and display the average price on the main screen.
• Color/Size:
If selected, the system opens a color and size-wise pricing pop-up where the user can define prices for each color and size combination. The system will calculate and display the average price on the main screen.
• Now user can select and de-select the color-size on the click of article-color-size where system will open the below given pop-up.
Columns:
• Color / Size
• Quantity
• Selling Price
• Value
• BOM
• Total Quantity

### 4.8 Instructions Section
This section captures operational and compliance-related instructions.

[TABLE 7: Table 7 · 6 rows · columns: Field Name (text) · identifiers: Field Name]
| Field Name |
| Trim Instructions |
| Wash Instructions |
| Testing Instructions |
| Fabric Instructions |
| Packing Instructions |
| Approval Instructions |

### 4.9 Documents Section

#### 4.9.1 Upload Options
Users can attach documents using:
• Copy & Paste
• Drag & Drop
• File Upload

#### 4.9.2 Document Management Grid
• Uploaded documents appear in a grid on the right side.
• Available actions:
• Preview document
• Delete document

### 4.10 History Section
This section maintains a complete audit trail of the Sales Order.

#### 4.10.1 History Types
• Revision History
• Approval History
• Cancellation History
• Approval Trial History

#### 4.10.2 Comments & Notes
• Displays comments and notes entered during the transaction creation
• Each entry includes:
• Date
• Time
• User Name

#### 4.10.3 Approval Trail
• This will show the approval hierarchy with their status and the comment which they had updated to the approval and rejection time.

## 5. Menu Permission and UI Navigations

### 5.1 Permission Navigation:
We need to introduce a new permission named Sales Order, which will include the following options:
• Sales Order – List
• Sales Order – New
In addition, in the last column, a view selection (dropdown/div option) should be provided. This option will open the views created through the View Configurator, allowing the user to select a buyer-wise view.
Note:
• The system should allow the selection of only one view per buyer.
Note: -
In the Sales Order Creation process, no separate view configuration permission is required. The system behaviour will be driven entirely by Buyer-level permissions.
Users will be able to select only those Buyers for which they have been granted access. Once a Buyer is selected, the system will automatically load the corresponding Sales Order Creation view mapped to that Buyer.
For Sales Order list: It should be radio button, user can permit only one view for a user

### 5.2 Menu Navigation
We also need to introduce a new submenu under the Sales menu named Sales Order, which will have the following options:
• List:
• This option will open the new Sales Order List user interface.
• New:
• This option will open the New Sales Order creation transaction interface.
In cases where both menu permissions (Old Sales Order and New Sales Order) are assigned to a user, the system behaviour should be as follows:
• The system should always open the New Sales Order List UI and the New Sales Order Creation UI by default.
• Users must create all new sales orders exclusively through the New Sales Order transaction.
However, for sales orders that were originally created using the old transaction (i.e., Purchase Order from Buyer transaction):
• These orders should appear in the New Sales Order List UI.
• When a user attempts to open such an order, it should always open in the Old Sales Order transaction UI.
• If the user performs any revision or amendment on these orders, the system should continue to open them in the Old transaction UI for all subsequent modifications.
Note: If no view is defined in the user permissions, the system should automatically apply the default view for those users.
We can made the multiple view for different-2 buyers, now if we permit the multiple view for various buyer to the single user then system should auto reflect the view based on the selection of buyer
